answer: An agent economy can anchor each identity to one real canal lock, where the keeper lives on its terrace and opens the gates for every passing boat. Each transit is logged under the vessel's voyage number, and random live checks demand the keeper work that lock on camera within minutes, so one operator cannot staff two locks at once. The night log is headed by the nebula visible overhead, and a license fee in outside money doubles per further lock on the same funding trail, so each extra fake costs another real lock, another keeper, another season of watches, and twice the prior fee.
